name: Front raise
pattern: Shoulder flexion: straight-ish arms lift forward to about shoulder height and lower again.
setup: Stand tall, weights in front of your thighs.
Palms facing your legs or each other, soft bend in the elbows.

steps.text: Lift the arms forward and up, keeping the elbows soft.
Stop at shoulder height, hands about level with your eyes at most.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.

cues.why: The front delt does most of the work up to about 90°; higher brings in the traps and serratus to rotate the shoulder blade.

cues.cue: Thumbs up or palms in feels best on the shoulder.
cues.why: Thumb-up (full can) arm positions load the cuff without the turned-in empty-can position.

cues.cue: No lean back or hip swing.
cues.why: Leaning back turns it into a swing and loads the lower back.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, let the shoulder blades glide naturally.
cues.why: The shoulder blade rotates up about 1° for every 2° of arm raise; shrugging adds upper-trap work instead.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

mistakes.name: Leaning back and swinging
mistakes.looks: The trunk rocks back and the hips push forward to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Stand still with a lighter weight, or sit or chest-support.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work and the lower back arches.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders hike up as the arms rise.
mistakes.fix: Shoulders down, stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.why: The upper trap takes the load.

mistakes.name: Elbows bend
mistakes.looks: Elbows bend more and more and the weight curls up.
mistakes.fix: Fix the elbow bend at about 10-20°.
mistakes.why: Shortens the lever and adds biceps.

safety: Shoulder pain: stop below 80° and use thumbs up.
Use light weights; the arm is a long lever.

variants.change: Both hands on one implement: palms down for a bar, palms in for a plate.
Cable from behind between the legs: tension at the bottom.
One arm: hold the trunk still.
Full can: arms 30° out from the front in the scapular plane, thumbs up.

variants.when: lateral to front|front and lateral|6 ways
variants.change: Combined raise: alternate side and front paths.
Palms up: a bit more biceps and upper chest.
Hold the arms at shoulder height.

subtypes.name: Front raise to overhead
subtypes.change: Keep raising past shoulder height until the arms are overhead.

subtypes.name: Incline chest-supported raise
subtypes.change: Lying face down on an incline bench about 45°, arms hang and lift forward to line up with the body.

subtypes.name: Lying front raise
subtypes.change: Lying on your back (bench or floor), lift the weight from over the thighs to over the chest: hardest at the start.

subtypes.name: Seated front raise
subtypes.change: Seated on a bench, no leg drive: same arm path.

motion.basis: Scapular upward rotation from the flexion ratio of about 2:1 and 46° total over full flexion in mcclure2001 (about 28° at 90° including a resting value, estimate); slight protraction during flexion is an estimate. Arm angles are by design (stop at shoulder height). Muscle emphasis from coratella2020 (frontal raise gave the highest anterior deltoid activity).

sources.cite: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Esposito F, Cè E. An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2020;17(17):6015.

Reinold MM, Macrina LC, Wilk KE, Fleisig GS, Dun S, Barrentine SW, Ellerbusch MT, Andrews JR. Electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises. J Athl Train. 2007;42(4):464-469.
McClure PW, Michener LA, Sennett BJ, Karduna AR. Direct 3-dimensional measurement of scapular kinematics during dynamic movements in vivo. J Shoulder Elbow Surg. 2001;10(3):269-277.
Haff GG, Triplett NT, eds. Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning. 4th ed. National Strength and Conditioning Association. Human Kinetics; 2016.
